title: Runtime Decision Replay and SLO Forensics Manual
author: Jordan Matthews
body:
Overview
========

This document describes the decision-replay pipeline and a structured forensic playbook for investigating SLO violations that originate in the serving runtime. It ties scheduler/kernel choices, KV cache hits/warmness, model variant routing, and cross-tenant admission decisions to downstream SLO impact. The goal is to provide a repeatable investigation path for engineers on-call and owners of runtime subsystems.

Scope
-----
- Applies to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private runtimes managed by the Redwood serving runtime.
- Focuses on latency and availability SLOs for synchronous generation / streaming endpoints (per-request SLOs: p50/p95/p99).
- Excludes model quality regressions; see quality-guardrails docs for signal correlation.

Key concepts and services
-------------------------
- runtime-dispatcher: front-line routing service that maps requests to execution slots and chooses model variants.
- slot-manager: tracks GPU resources and admission credits across heterogeneous pools.
- kernel-orchestrator: selects kernel/attention plan and preemption policy per request.
- kvcache-proxy: global KV cache coordinator for prefix and session caches; exposes cache_warmness metadata.
- replay-indexer: storage + query layer for deterministic decision replays (see Decision Replay format section).

Required telemetry and artifacts (must be present for replay)
---------------------------------------------------------
1) request-trace (full event timeline, request_id) — retention: 30d
2) scheduler-decision-record (slot, priority, preemption_token) — retention: 90d
3) kernel-hint-record (kernel_id, tile_plan, estimated_cycles) — retention: 90d
4) kvcache-stats (hit/miss, warmness, evicted_keys) — retention: 7d (aggregates) / 30d (per-session)
5) system-metrics at 1s resolution (GPU utilization, mem pressure, nvlink errors) — retention: 14d
6) request-payload (prompt length, sequence length, truncated flag) — retention: 7d

Decision Replay format (canonical JSON)
--------------------------------------
A single replay bundle is stored as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each line is a flat object, sample keys below; the replay-indexer exposes a /replay API that returns NDJSON to feed local deterministic replays. Example snippet: 

{
  "request_id": "r-20251201-6843",
  "timestamp": "2025-12-01T14:23:45.123Z",
  "dispatcher_decision": "pool-a:slot-42",
  "kernel_choice": "matmul-tiling-v3",
  "kvcache_warmness": "cold",
  "estimated_tokens": "512",
  "observed_latency_ms": "1245"
}

(Keep fields flat and string-typed to simplify ingestion across languages.)

Triggering conditions for a forensics replay
-------------------------------------------
- Automated: SLO alert fires (p95 or p99 breach sustained for 5m) and the incident playbook triggers replay-indexer ingestion.
- Manual: engineer on-call suspects an event (e.g., sudden p95 spike correlated with kernel rollout). Use the manual replay steps below.

Forensic investigation playbook (step-by-step)
----------------------------------------------
1) Triage and scope (5–15 minutes)
   - Pull the SLO alert timeline from alerting-dashboard (time window T = alert start - 10m to alert end + 10m).
   - Identify a representative set of request_ids (prefer p99 offenders and a small sample of p95/p50).
   - Record business impact: request types, customers affected, percent traffic impacted.

2) Bulk metadata unlock (5 minutes)
   - Query replay-indexer for the request_ids: /api/v1/replay?ids=r-...
   - Confirm required artifacts exist for each request (scheduler record, kernel hint, kv state). If missing, mark as partial replay; annotate possible blind spots.

3) Deterministic local replay (10–30 minutes)
   - Use the replay harness (runtime-replayer CLI) which accepts NDJSON. Example: runtime-replayer --input bundle.ndjson --mode dry-run
   - Validate the harness reproduces the observed kernel_choice and dispatcher_decision. If divergence occurs, capture the divergence snapshot: 
     - runtime-replayer --input bundle.ndjson --emit-divergence=divergence.log

4) Attribution pass (30–60 minutes)
   - Compare baseline vs observed: create a delta matrix across factors: kvcache_warmness, kernel_choice, slot_latency, preemption events.
   - Use the causal scoring heuristic (see table below) to rank likely root causes.

5) Hypothesis testing (minutes to hours)
   - If kvcache coldness is top candidate: re-run replay with kvcache_warmness forced to "warm" and measure simulated latency delta.
   - If kernel_choice is suspect: re-run with previous kernel (kernel-v2) and compare per-step cycle counts.
   - If scheduling/preemption suspected: re-run multiple requests in a batch to surface contention effects.

6) Remediation and rollback (variable)
   - If a kernel rollout caused regression: open an urgent kernel-rollback PR to kernel-orchestrator and schedule canary rollback.
   - If admission policy misconfiguration: update slot-manager policy and monitor SLOs for 30m.

Causal scoring heuristic (illustrative)
-------------------------------------
Score factors (0-100 each):
- kvcache_delta_score: function(hit_rate_change, warmness)
- kernel_regress_score: function(est_cycles_increase, memory_pressure)
- schedule_contention_score: function(queue_depth_change, preemptions)
- infra_fault_score: function(nvlink_errors, gpu_throttle_count)

Rank = weighted_sum([kvcache:0.25, kernel:0.35, schedule:0.25, infra:0.15])

Quick reference SLO thresholds (applies to core-generation-route)
---------------------------------------------------------------
| SLO metric        | Target   | Alert threshold          | Escalation window | Owner          |
|-------------------|----------|-------------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| p50 latency       | 60ms     | >120ms for 5m           | Pager (P1)        | runtime-sre    |
| p95 latency       | 220ms    | >350ms for 3m           | Pager (P0)        | runtime-sre    |
| p99 latency       | 850ms    | >1200ms sustained 2m    | Pager (P0)        | runtime-sre    |
| availability      | 99.95%   | drop 0.2% in 1h         | Incident (P0)     | runtime-sre    |

(These thresholds are per-route and subject to per-customer SLA overrides; always check route-level overrides in token-config DB.)

Common root causes and signposts
--------------------------------
- Cold KV cache (signs: kvcache_warmness==cold, cluster-wide recent evictions, per-session miss spikes)
- Kernel regression (signs: kernel_hint shows new kernel id, estimated_cycles >> baseline, p95 increase tied to rollout window)
- Admission pressure (signs: queue_depth spike, preemption_count increment, allocation_timeouts)
- Infra flakiness (signs: nvlink/PCIe errors, GPU thermal throttling alarms)
- Telemetry sampling artifacts (signs: trace gaps, missing scheduler records)

Playbook checklists and commands
-------------------------------
- Commands:
  1) Fetch replay bundle: curl -sS "https://replay-indexer.internal/replay?range=2026-02-09T10:00:00Z,2026-02-09T11:00:00Z&route=core-gen" > bundle.ndjson
  2) Run deterministic replay: runtime-replayer --input bundle.ndjson --log-level debug --emit-metrics
  3) Query kv cache state: redis-cli -h kvcache-proxy-01 info | grep Evicted
  4) Inspect kernel rollout timeline: ksctl rollout history kernel-orchestrator | tail -n 50

- Minimal investigation checklist (tick-box):
  - [ ] Representative p99 request_ids collected
  - [ ] Replay bundle exists and replays without missing artifacts
  - [ ] Divergence snapshot captured (if any)
  - [ ] Ranked causal candidates and hypothesis list documented in incident ticket
  - [ ] Remediation planned and annotated with rollback plan

Testing the replay pipeline (how to validate a new trace source)
----------------------------------------------------------------
1) Add synthetic trace producer: runtime-test-harness can emit controlled divergence scenarios (flags: --fault kvcache-evict --burst 100).
2) Run in staging: inject 1K synthetic requests from the harness for 30s.
3) Validate replay-indexer stores NDJSON bundles and the runtime-replayer reproduces the divergence.
4) Add a unit test in replay-indexer that asserts schema completeness for required keys.

Operating agreements and ownership
----------------------------------
- runtime-sre: incident lead and primary pager for production SLO breaches. Responsible for running this playbook during incidents.
- runtime-serving: owner for dispatcher_decision logic, kernel-orchestrator changes, and rollout gating.
- infra-stability: owns hardware-related investigations (nvlink, thermal, EC errors).
- telemetry-platform: maintain replay-indexer SLAs (ingest latency <30s) and schema stability.

Rollout guidance for changes that affect decision-collapse surface
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Always include a deterministic replay diff in PRs that touch dispatcher, slot-manager, or kernel-orchestrator. The PR template must include: before.ndjson, after.ndjson, and a 1-page summary of delta.
- Canary policy: run kernel and dispatcher changes at 0.5% traffic for 30 minutes, compare causal score distributions.

Appendix A: Example incident timeline (annotated)
------------------------------------------------
1) 10:03 UTC - Alert: p99 latency exceeds 1200ms
2) 10:04 UTC - runtime-sre triage: fetch 200 p99 request_ids
3) 10:06 UTC - replay-indexer returns bundle; 40% of reqs missing kvcache state -> mark partial
4) 10:12 UTC - deterministic replay shows kernel-v3 increased estimated_cycles by 2.8x relative to baseline
5) 10:22 UTC - rollback of kernel-v3 to v2 initiated; p99 improves toward baseline within 12 minutes

Appendix B: Troubleshooting tips
--------------------------------
- If replay diverges immediately: check schema version mismatches between runtime and replay-indexer (header field: replay_schema_v).
- If kvcache artifacts missing for customers on Private deployments: confirm replay-agent sidecar is enabled in the customer manifest.
- If preemption_count is high but queues are not deep: investigate cross-tenant quota bleed; consult tenant-throttle logs.

References and related reading
----------------------------
- runtime-dispatcher design doc (internal link): /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/delta-routing-and-cost-partitioning-architecture-2026
- Kernel rollout policy: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-handshake-and-adaptive-fallback-patterns-2026
- SLO runbook canonical page: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/p99-slo-handbook

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary on-call: runtime-sre rotation (pager duty team: @runtime-sre)
- Slack channels: #runtime-ops, #kernel-rollouts, #kvcache
- Emergency escalation path: runtime-sre -> Head of Infra -> CTO (as per incident policy)
